rationale: The Latin anchors *intumescere* ("to swell up") and *tumida æquora* ("swelling/swollen seas") firmly point to the sense of swelling or enlarging, which corresponds directly to puff.v.07 ("to swell or cause to enlarge"). The Old English verb *a-þindan* means "to swell up/puff up" (e.g., of bodily swelling in the Herbal, and of swelling waves in the Psalter quotation), ruling out any respiratory or metaphorical senses.
